g.text: samtal: one conversation turn, from wake word to spoken reply
Before the first turn (once per boot, once per connection)
Persisted to NVS. samtal-server serves no
firmware images, so the firmware section
always answers "up to date", and the reply
A failure is an HTTP 403 on the upgrade,
which stock firmware retries and refreshes.
hello (audio params, device MAC, client id)
Ten seconds each way, then the session gives up.
The device is resolved to an agent here; a device
bound to no agent is told so and closed.
Discovery runs as a background task,
so a first utterance never waits on it.
Flow 1: from the voice to the model
The speaker and the microphone sit centimetres
apart, so the microphone hears the assistant too.
subtracts the known playback before anything
else runs. It is what makes barge-in possible.
binary Opus frames, 16 kHz, 60 ms each
(v1 bare packets; v2 and v3 prefix a header)
decode to PCM, s16le mono 16 kHz
A continuously listening device piles silence in
front of every utterance. Only the endpointer knows
where the speech began, so it reports the offset and
the session cuts there rather than transcribing the
wait. The buffer is bounded: a realtime session
listens through the silences for the whole session.
`lock_language` is the provider asking the session
to reuse a language for the rest of the session.
It is how a per-session policy lives in a provider
that is shared between sessions and holds no
The reply: a tool loop the session owns
The loop lives in the session, not in a provider,
because only the session can change agents between
rounds. Up to MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 4; the last round is
sent with tool_choice = "none", so a reply always
ends in speech rather than in a tool nobody hears.
A failure is a result too: the model
phrases what to tell the user, in its
own voice and the user's language.
Flow 2: from the model's words to the ears
punctuation once the whitespace has arrived
PCM chunks at the voice's rate
resample to 24 kHz, encode 60 ms Opus,
Synthesizing only after a sentence finished playing puts
its whole time to first byte on the speaker as silence,
once per sentence: measured at 617 ms and 520 ms on a
three-sentence reply, and reported from a board session
as "hiccups in the assistant's voice". Running ahead
spends that time against playback already happening.
so the paced consumer keeps its backpressure on a provider
that can produce far faster than realtime.
The device asked once and never stopped streaming,
so the session never stops listening. It therefore
hears the user through its own reply, which is
(120 s by default) hangs up a realtime session,
which would otherwise hold a slot forever.
